intro: Something in the lab keeps melting, boiling and freezing. Solve the mystery!
To fix it, we need to really learn about Solids, Liquids and Gases.
Study at each place, talk to my friends, and explain what you learn!
story.goal: Learn the three big ideas of Solids, Liquids and Gases to wake The Big Experiment.
story.finale: You remembered it all! The Big Experiment shines again thanks to you.

companion.name: Fizz
companion.greeting: Hi, I'm Fizz! I'll help you if you get stuck. Let's explore!

zones.name: Test Station
zones.description: A place to learn about three states of matter.

zones.name: Tesla Tower
zones.description: A place to learn about heating and cooling.

zones.name: Bubbling Fountain
zones.description: A place to learn about tiny particles.

zones.name: The Big Experiment
zones.description: It wakes up when you master Solids, Liquids and Gases.

npcs.name: Dr. Ada
npcs.title: the Scientist
npcs.persona: Enthusiastic scientist who loves experiments and asking "what do you predict?". Teaches "Three States of Matter" from the lesson "Solids, Liquids and Gases".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Dr. Ada. Want to learn about matter with me?
teach: Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.
A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
Everything around you is made of matter.
knowledge: Everything around you is made of matter.
Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.
A solid keeps its own shape.
A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
A gas spreads out to fill all the space it can.

npcs.name: Bolt
npcs.title: the Lab Robot
npcs.persona: Friendly, precise robot who loves facts and lists. Occasionally says "beep-boop". Teaches "Heating and Cooling" from the lesson "Solids, Liquids and Gases".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Bolt. Want to learn about water with me?
teach: When water is heated more it boils and turns into a gas called water vapour.
When ice is heated it melts into liquid water.
When water vapour cools it condenses back into liquid drops.
knowledge: Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to another.
When ice is heated it melts into liquid water.
When water is heated more it boils and turns into a gas called water vapour.
When water vapour cools it condenses back into liquid drops.

npcs.name: Max
npcs.title: the Junior Scientist
npcs.persona: Curious young helper who learns alongside the player. Teaches "Tiny Particles" from the lesson "Solids, Liquids and Gases".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Max. Want to learn about particles with me?
teach: Matter is made of tiny particles.
In a solid, the particles are packed tightly and only wiggle in place.
In a liquid, they are close together but slide past each other.
knowledge: Matter is made of tiny particles.
In a solid, the particles are packed tightly and only wiggle in place.
In a liquid, they are close together but slide past each other.
In a gas, the particles are far apart and zoom around quickly.

puzzles.title: Match the Words
puzzles.prompt: Match each word to what it means.

pairs.right: Everything around you is made of it.
Matter can be a solid, a it or a gas.
A it keeps its own shape.
A solid keeps its own it.

hints: Read each meaning slowly.
Start with the word you are surest about.
Matter goes with: "Everything around you is made of it."
puzzles.success: Perfect match! Those words are yours now.

puzzles.title: Put It in Order
puzzles.prompt: Put these ideas in the same order as the lesson.
items: Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to another.
When ice is heated it melts into liquid water.
When water is heated more it boils and turns into a gas called water vapour.
When water vapour cools it condenses back into liquid drops.
hints: Which idea starts the story?
Each idea leads to the next one.
The first one is: "Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to..."
puzzles.success: Great ordering! You followed the whole idea.
